claims.text: Changing Pt–Pd alloy composition shifts the surface-atom d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
The d-band center governs the adsorption energies of ORR intermediates.
An optimally positioned d-band center produces moderate binding and balanced adsorption–desorption kinetics.
Balanced adsorption–desorption kinetics enhance ORR activity relative to pure Pt.
Balanced adsorption–desorption kinetics lower peroxide formation and thereby improve ORR selectivity relative to pure Pt.
Balanced adsorption–desorption kinetics enhance catalyst durability and cycling stability relative to pure Pt.
Pt80Pd20 or Pt60Pd40 will exhibit greater ORR activity than pure Pt under otherwise identical conditions.
Pt80Pd20 or Pt60Pd40 will produce less peroxide than pure Pt under otherwise identical conditions.
Pt80Pd20 or Pt60Pd40 will retain performance better during cycling than pure Pt.
Pure Pd has an excessively shifted d-band center and will perform worse than the proposed intermediate Pt–Pd compositions.
The proposed composition effect applies when adsorbate binding energy is a key kinetic descriptor for ORR.
The proposed interpretation requires particle size, support effects, and surface composition to be controlled.
Minor morphology differences or surface segregation may influence the measured catalytic behavior despite the proposed controls.
A correlation between measured d-band-center shifts and ORR metrics is expected across the Pt–Pd composition series.

contradictions.description: The intervention says the controls will ensure that catalytic changes arise solely from d-band-center shifts, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that uncontrolled morphology variation or surface segregation may also influence behavior.
